allow: Scratchpad Operations: Creating, deleting, moving, or unpacking files anywhere under the Claude scratchpad (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\claude\**) is local work, including `rm -rf`, `unzip`, and downloading release archives there with `gh release download`. Downloading or unpacking an archive is not an install.

Headless Probe: Starting a program in the background with its input and output redirected (`</dev/null >/dev/null`, `--logging=<file>`, `--server-name <x> --remote-expr`) in order to read its startup log or query it, and quitting that same instance through its own remote command or by a PID this session started, is investigation, not session interference. This exception does not cover a launch that opens a window the user sees or writes outside the scratchpad.

Dotfiles via chezmoi: Editing files under the user's chezmoi source directory (`~/.local/share/chezmoi`) and running `chezmoi apply|diff|status|managed|data|verify` is this user's routine dotfiles workflow, not scope escalation.
soft_deny: Software Install [named+specifics — **must name:** the program being installed or removed]: Installing, uninstalling, or upgrading software on this machine through a package manager or installer — `winget install|uninstall|upgrade`, `scoop install|uninstall|update|reset`, `brew install|uninstall`, `pip|pipx|uv tool install`, `npm i -g`, `cargo install`, `mise install|use`, or running a downloaded `*-setup.exe`, `.msi`, `.pkg`. Clears when the user named that program for install or removal in this transcript. A request to research, compare, verify, or check a program does not clear it, and the agent's own proposal to install it is not user intent.

Persistent Environment [named+specifics — **must name:** the variable or key, or the program it configures]: Writing persistent user or machine environment variables or registry values — `setx`, `reg add|delete|import`, `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable`, `Set-ItemProperty` under `HKCU:\Environment` — or registering services, scheduled tasks, or login items. Clears when the user named the variable or key, or when the user asked in this transcript to install or configure the program that the variable exists to configure. A variable that changes PATH, the shell, or the editor for every program is never cleared by naming one program.

Out-of-Scope Local Files [named+specifics — **must name:** the file or directory, or the program whose configuration it is]: Deleting, moving, renaming, or overwriting files or directories that this session did not create, outside the Claude scratchpad, the working directory, the user's chezmoi source directory (`~/.local/share/chezmoi`), `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp`, and `/tmp` — for example under `%APPDATA%`, `%USERPROFILE%`, `~/.config`, `/etc`. A directory that a program launched by this session created or recreated counts as not created by the session. Clears when the user named the path, or asked in this transcript to install, configure, clean up, or remove the program whose configuration directory it is.

Process Kill by Name [named+specifics — **must name:** the program]: Terminating processes by image or process name — `taskkill /IM`, `taskkill /F /IM`, `pkill`, `killall`, `Stop-Process -Name` — when the user has not named that program in this transcript. A kill by name also reaches instances the user is running in their own terminal. Clears when the user named the program for install, configuration, stop, or removal. Killing a PID this session started, or quitting an instance through its own remote command, is not this rule.

Live Session Interference [named+specifics — **must name:** the user's terminal, window, or pane and the action]: Creating tabs or panes, sending keystrokes or text, closing panes, or moving focus in a terminal, editor, or window the user is using — `wezterm cli spawn|send-text|kill-pane|split-pane|activate-pane|activate-tab`, `wezterm start`, `tmux send-keys|new-window|kill-pane|kill-window`, `osascript`, `xdotool`, `SendKeys` — and launching a TUI or GUI program the user will see (`start`, `explorer`, `open`, or a curses program on a pty). The user's live session is not a test fixture. Asking to install, try, check, or verify a program does not clear this. Clears when the user named their terminal or window and the action. Once the user has named their terminal for this task, spawning panes there and sending keys to the panes this session created are part of that permission; sending keys to a pane the user was already using still needs the user to name that pane.
